message.content:
Based on my search, I can provide you with comprehensive information about food acceptance temperatures. The term "food acceptance temperature" typically refers to the temperatures at which food should be received/accepted during delivery, as well as safe temperatures for consuming food.

## Food Receiving/Acceptance Temperatures

When accepting food deliveries, certain temperature requirements must be met:

### Cold Foods
- **Cold TCS (Time/Temperature Control for Safety) foods** must be received at **41°F (5°C) or below**
- **Frozen foods** must be received frozen solid (typically **32°F/0°C or lower**, ideally at **0°F/-18°C**)

### Hot Foods
- **Hot TCS foods** must be received at **135°F (57°C) or above**

According to Minnesota Department of Health guidelines: *"If food temperatures do not meet requirements or if TCS food shows evidence of previous temperature abuse, do not accept the food, or discard the products."*

## Safe Food Temperature Zones

| Category | Temperature | Notes |
|----------|-------------|-------|
| **Temperature Danger Zone** | 40°F - 140°F (4°C - 60°C) | Bacteria multiply rapidly; food should not be in this zone for more than 2 hours (1 hour if above 90°F/32°C ambient) |
| **Cold Holding** | 41°F (5°C) or below | For refrigerated foods |
| **Hot Holding** | 135°F (57°C) or above | For cooked foods being kept warm |
| **Safe Serving Temperature (Hot)** | 140°F - 165°F (60°C - 74°C) | Minimum safe temperatures for consumption |

## Safe Minimum Internal Cooking Temperatures for Consumption

| Food Type | Minimum Internal Temperature |
|-----------|------------------------------|
| Poultry (all types) | 165°F (74°C) |
| Ground meats (beef, pork, lamb) | 160°F (71°C) |
| Whole cuts of beef, pork, lamb, veal | 145°F (63°C) + 3 min rest |
| Fish and seafood | 145°F (63°C) |
| Egg dishes | 160°F (71°C) |
| Leftovers and reheated foods | 165°F (74°C) |
| Cooked vegetables | 135°F (57°C) |

## Key Points for Food Acceptance

1. **Always use a thermometer** - Never rely on appearance alone
2. **Reject deliveries** that don't meet temperature requirements
3. **Check frozen foods** - They should be solid with no signs of thawing
4. **Document temperatures** at receiving for food safety records
5. **Move quickly** - Get perishable foods into proper storage within 2 hours

Sources:
1. https://ladle.com/resources/blog/safe-food-temperatures-protect-public-health-and-your-bottom-line/
2. https://www.foodsafety.gov/food-safety-charts/safe-minimum-internal-temperatures
3. https://foodblogga.com/food-safety/safe-temperature-range-for-storing-food/
4. https://alwaysfoodsafe.com/es/proper-food-temperatures
5. https://www.health.state.mn.us/communities/environment/food/docs/fs/tcsfoodfs.pdf
6. https://www.tcrentalsolutions.com/blog/temperature-in-food-safety
7. https://essentialfoodhygiene.co.uk/the-correct-temperature-to-serve-hot-foods-explained/
